## Manual agents and why

- **Roo Code** (`roo`) — User-scope MCP path is VS-Code-global-storage-dependent (unverified); context/skills paths above are verified — wire those by hand or via npx skills.
- **Kilo Code** (`kilo`) — Global MCP.json path undocumented and settings are JSONC; not safely mergeable with stdlib-only JSON tooling.
- **Goose** (`goose`) — MCP config is YAML; a stdlib-only merge would be fragile. Context is project-scope only.
- **Aider** (`aider`) — No context auto-discovery (config is YAML), no MCP support, no skills support — printed instructions only.
- **Warp** (`warp`) — MCP managed via GUI with undocumented backing file; no user-scope context file — printed instructions only.
- **Hermes Agent** (`hermes`) — MCP config is YAML (~/.hermes/config.yaml); stdlib-only merge would be fragile. Context is workspace-scope only.
- **OpenHands** (`openhands`) — No stable user-scope MCP config file to merge (UI/CLI-managed); context is repo-scope — printed instructions only.
- **Google Jules** (`jules`) — Web/GitHub cloud agent — nothing local to configure; commit AGENTS.md to your repos instead.

## Notes

- Detection: a binary on PATH (e.g. `codex`) or an existing config path under `~` (e.g. `~/.codex`). `--only`/`--skip` override detection per id.
- All renderers preserve unrelated keys and user entries; every modified file gets a timestamped `.bak` sibling first. Env entries are `${VAR}` name placeholders — never values.
- Windows equivalents: most `~/.config/...` tools use the same path under the user profile; Zed uses `{appdata}\Zed`. Unverified per-Windows paths default to the POSIX path.
- Sources: every entry was verified against the vendor documentation linked in the Agent column (2026-10 audit).
